name: Nakamura-Voss NV-7 Patrol Vest
description:
A tactical vest worn by private security contractors and building security throughout the mid-tiers. Constructed from a dense ballistic-weave nylon with soft armor panels integrated into the front and back — rated for low-velocity rounds and blade resistance, though Nakamura-Voss is careful never to make specific performance claims in their marketing materials. MOLLE webbing runs along the chest and sides for attachment of pouches and accessories. Available in black, slate grey, and a dark navy used by several corponation security divisions.

The NV-7 is the visual shorthand for 'armed private security' throughout GLMZ. It reads as authority in the mid-tiers and as threat in the Shelf. The soft armor panels are removable for laundering, and the vest itself is reasonably comfortable for all-day wear — a small mercy for the people who spend twelve-hour shifts in them.
functionality: Integrated soft armor front and back panels rated for low-velocity ballistic and blade threats. Panels are removable and replaceable.
what_it_says: You are armed, employed in a security capacity, and you want that to be immediately visible.
worn_by: off-duty security who forgot to change
some Tier 2 residents in dangerous neighborhoods who've acquired them secondhand
story_hooks: A shipment of NV-7 vests was diverted before reaching a corporate client — they've shown up in a Shelf neighborhood, which means someone is arming up for something.
The replacement armor panels sold officially are standard-rated; a black-market supplier is selling panels with significantly higher ratings using stolen corponation materials.
A security contractor was shot while wearing a properly certified NV-7 — the round went through. Someone has been quietly swapping real panels for dummy inserts in the supply chain.

physical_description.visual_profile: A structured, utilitarian silhouette that projects immediate authority. The vest sits squarely on the shoulders with defined edges at the armholes, creating a blocky, imposing profile. The soft armor panels underneath create subtle dimensional bulges across the chest and back, preventing a completely flat appearance. Multiple rows of MOLLE webbing create a grid-like texture across the torso.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed and deliberately oversized through the chest to accommodate soft armor panels and layering. Cut to sit clear of the body without being baggy—engineered for all-day wearability and quick movement. Adjustable side straps with friction-fit closures allow customization for different body types and heavy gear loads.
physical_description.primary_material: Dense ballistic-weave nylon with integrated modular soft armor panels (polyethylene composite). The exterior is ripstop-treated nylon for durability. Armor panels are removable for maintenance.
physical_description.texture: The outer surface is smooth but subtly gridded from the underlying MOLLE webbing. Armor panels create a slightly raised, quilted appearance where they're laminated into pockets. The nylon has a soft sheen under direct light, with a slightly waxy feel from weatherproofing treatment.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primarily matte black with slate grey and dark navy variants. Accents include black plastic hardware and dark olive-drab friction straps. Manufacturer branding (Nakamura-Voss logo) is typically minimal and gray-on-black, positioned center chest.
physical_description.closures: Double-width main zipper down the front (heavy-gauge, tactical-grade), reinforced with friction-fit side straps with climbing-style buckles. Shoulder straps can be adjusted via velcro tabs.
distinctive_features: MOLLE webbing across chest and sides for modular pouch attachment
Removable soft armor panels (front and back rated for low-velocity impact and blade resistance)
Reinforced stitching along all seams with bar-tacks at stress points
Internal mesh lining visible through the front zipper for breathability
Minimalist Nakamura-Voss wordmark and logo (center chest, gray embroidery)
Multiple small loops and D-rings for equipment attachment
Slightly longer rear tail for additional coverage when seated
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 boundary. Accessible to mid-tier security contractors and corpo divisions, signaling competence and training rather than luxury. Ubiquitous enough to be recognized as standard-issue, not aspirational.
physical_description.cultural_context: The uniform of armed private security, building protection, and low-level corpo enforcement. Wearing it identifies the wearer as someone with authority to enforce rules on corporate or contracted property. On the Shelf (Tier 5), it reads as a threat or as evidence of collaboration.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn-in but well-maintained. Regular users keep it clean and functional, with possible wear on the zipper pull and minor scuffing on the armor panel edges. Dust and minor stains from urban environments are common. Some patches or replaced straps may appear on older units.
